finalPass.decision:
All four candidates stand as real. #0 is the one that matters: four repo-root scripts that WRITE rounded money values still carry private roundMoney copies anchored only by a comment naming a file this PR deletes, and every gate the PR installs (codemod, no-mirrors tripwire, body-diff) is scoped to skip scripts/ — ruled major because it leaves the consolidation's riskiest callers ungated, though it is not a behavioral regression. #1 (stale mirror assertions in two app files the codemod itself edited), #2 (the package's lint script is a tsc alias, so the single money source is now outside ESLint), and #3 (the T4 guard's docblock and L-054 overclaim generality while the main check is hardcoded; the toEqual pin fails closed but the docs steer the next author wrong) are all real and minor. The read covered the 22 HIGH-risk files well but stopped at the package boundary; three build-time interactions were never exercised and each could break a green tree silently — turbo's ^build wiring for the edit-then-verify loop now that the mirror-inputs block is gone, the api/web Dockerfile COPY-before-npm-ci ordering with the new postinstall (only mobile's was ruled on), and Metro's resolution of the mobile app's first runtime workspace import. Each is one bounded read.
Second read: All four second-read candidates are real but minor: one more tripwire blind spot (the T4 runtime-import guard cannot see CommonJS `require`/`import =`/dynamic `import()` forms that the api source already uses), and three turbo task-graph edges around the new compiled package — `lint` lacks the `^build` edge that every other task carries, `pricing#dev` and `pricing#build` race over the same `dist/` on `npm run dev`, and `@routeflow/api#test` now reads `apps/mobile/jest.config.js` outside its cache inputs (a sibling of the already-confirmed `pricing#test` stale-cache finding, best fixed together by restoring an explicit inputs block). None of them changes money bodies or breaks a build today; each is a small, mechanical hardening the fixer should fold in with the open turbo.json and tripwire work. The named gaps from the first read (turbo graph, api/web Dockerfile staging, Metro resolution) were covered by this read and produced no blocker, so the run closes here with no further reads.

Nothing this PR adds can see them. packages/pricing/src/no-mirrors.spec.ts:461 sets `SCAN_ROOTS = ["apps/api/src", "apps/api/scripts", "apps/api/test", "apps/web", "apps/mobile"]` — the repo-root `scripts/` tree is not a scan root, and IMPORT_PATTERNS (:467-474) only match quoted import specifiers, never a local function definition. scripts/codemods/pricing-import-rewrite.mjs rewrites import specifiers only. Meanwhile CLAUDE.md's rewritten money-discipline section and .claude/code-map now both assert 'All line/tax/total math lives in packages/pricing … there are no mirrors', and .claude/campaign/status/F04.jsonl's own B122 row records the fix radius as 'all three mirrors + both script copies' — the phrase that made the script copies visible is exactly the structure this PR retires.

Failure scenario: a follow-up changes the cent-rounding policy in packages/pricing/src/pricing.ts:638 — precisely what REG-B122 already did once (EPSILON nudge -> toFixed(4) decimal re-render, which moved 2.135 from 2.13 to 2.14). Every app surface picks it up through the single import. scripts/repair-integrity.mjs keeps the old body, and an owner runs it against production to reconcile invoice totals; on any line whose value lands on an exact half-cent the script writes a total one cent below what the API computes for the same line — re-introducing the API-vs-stored divergence the script exists to repair, and doing so with the DB write, not a report. The no-mirrors tripwire stays green, the golden table stays green, `npm run verify` stays green, and CLAUDE.md tells the next agent there are no mirrors to check.
findings.fixHint: Either add the repo-root `scripts/` tree to no-mirrors.spec.ts's SCAN_ROOTS with a rounding-policy equality check (assert each script's roundMoney body matches the package's), or re-point the four comments at `@routeflow/pricing#roundMoney` and record in CLAUDE.md that these four zero-import scripts are a deliberate, gated exception rather than claiming 'there are no mirrors'.
findings.decision: The evidence shows four write-path scripts (three repair-* writers plus feature-smoke) each carrying a private cent-rounding copy whose only correctness anchor was a comment naming apps/api/src/common/pricing.ts, which this PR deletes; the no-mirrors tripwire and the codemod both exclude scripts/, so the PR's single-source guarantee leaves the DB-writing copies ungated with a dangling source of truth. findings.summary: The repo's single money source is now outside ESLint entirely — its `lint` script is an alias for `check-types`, so `turbo run lint` reports green having run zero lint rules on pricing.ts.
findings.detail:
packages/pricing/package.json declares `"lint": "tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json"` and `"check-types": "tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json"` — byte-identical commands. `npm run lint` (= `turbo run lint`, per the root package.json) therefore executes the type checker twice and never runs ESLint over packages/pricing/src/pricing.ts or tier-pricing.ts.

Before this PR all four money sources were ESLint-covered: apps/api/src/common/pricing.ts and apps/api/src/utils/pricing.ts through apps/api/package.json's `eslint "{src,apps,libs,test}/**/*.ts"` with eslint.config.mjs's `eslint.configs.recommended` + `tseslint.configs.recommendedTypeChecked`; apps/web/lib/pricing.ts through `next lint`; apps/mobile/lib/pricing.ts through `eslint . --ext .ts,.tsx`. All 4 files now consolidate into one file that no ESLint config reaches.

What is actually lost is the `eslint.configs.recommended` core set that tsc does not duplicate. Concretely, `no-fallthrough`: packages/typescript-config/base.json (read this session) sets `strict: true` but not `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, and packages/pricing/tsconfig.json does not add it. computeCategoryTax (packages/pricing/src/pricing.ts:916-934) is built on an intentional three-case fall-through (EXCISE_PER_UNIT / PER_VOLUME / DEPOSIT_PER_CONTAINER share one `return roundMoney(rate * basisQty)`). Add a statement under `case "EXCISE_PER_UNIT":` and forget the `break`, and the excise levy silently also runs the per-volume path; the API copy would have failed lint with `no-fallthrough` as an error, and now nothing static catches it — only whichever golden/unit assertions happen to cover that exact taxType. The same gap covers `no-unsafe-*`, `no-constant-condition`, `no-dupe-keys` and the rest of the recommended set on the file every money value in the product flows through. `packages/types` sets the same lint=tsc precedent, but it holds type declarations, not executable money logic.
findings.fixHint: Give packages/pricing a real flat ESLint config (packages/eslint-config/base.js is already a workspace dep pattern) and set `"lint": "eslint . --max-warnings 0"`, or at minimum add `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` + `noUnusedLocals` to packages/pricing/tsconfig.json so the alias is not a silent downgrade.
findings.decision: packages/pricing/package.json's lint script is byte-identical to check-types, so turbo run lint reports green having run zero ESLint rules on the consolidated money source, whereas all four predecessor files were ESLint-covered. A genuine coverage loss introduced by the PR, but lint is not correctness.

findings.summary: The T4 guard's docblock and lesson L-054 both promise it checks "every @routeflow/<name> the API imports has a built main", but the only main check is hardcoded to @routeflow/pricing.
findings.detail:
The docblock at apps/api/src/common/no-runtime-workspace-imports.spec.ts:46-52 states: 'every `@routeflow/<name>` package the API value-imports from a compiled source file must ship a built (`.js`) `main`'. .claude/lessons/LESSONS.md L-054's Guard line repeats it: 'this PR makes it assert every `@routeflow/*` the API imports has a built `main`.'

The implementation does not generalise. `collectRuntimeWorkspacePackages` (:53-73) does collect every `@routeflow/*` value-import, but the test at :76-79 only pins the collected list to `toEqual(["@routeflow/pricing"])`, and the main check at :81-94 does not consume that list at all — it hardcodes `require.resolve("@routeflow/pricing/package.json")` (:84) and asserts that one manifest's `main` matches `/\.js$/`.

Failure scenario: a later PR adds a second compiled workspace package the API imports at runtime (e.g. a shared FX or tax package). The :76 test fails with `["@routeflow/newpkg","@routeflow/pricing"] !== ["@routeflow/pricing"]`, and the obvious repair — add the new name to the expected array — makes the suite green again while running zero main-is-compiled verification for it. If that package ships source-direct like @routeflow/types (`main: "./index.ts"`), `nest build` emits `require("@routeflow/newpkg")` verbatim and `node dist/main.js` dies at startup parsing the .ts — the exact whole-API outage L-054 and the file's own opening docblock (:1-14) exist to prevent, with a green guard and a lesson entry that told the author it was covered. A lesson is a durable rule other agents plan from, so the over-claim propagates.

(Not reported as a defect but verified while checking this: the walker at :27 uses `/\.tsx?$/`, which does include .tsx, so apps/api/src/invoices/invoice-pdf-template.tsx IS scanned.)
findings.fixHint: Make the main check iterate `collectRuntimeWorkspacePackages(SRC_ROOT)` with `it.each`/a loop instead of hardcoding @routeflow/pricing at :84, then either keep the exact-list pin as a separate allowlist assertion or drop it; if the generalisation is deliberately out of scope, correct the :46-52 docblock and L-054's Guard line to say the guard forbids any second runtime workspace import rather than verifying one.
findings.decision: The docblock and L-054 promise a general 'every @routeflow/* has a built main' check while the code hardcodes @routeflow/pricing; the toEqual pin on the collected list does fail closed when a second package appears, so the next author is forced to touch the test, but the misleading doc and lesson make it likely they extend the array without extending the main check.

findings.summary: The new T4/R6 runtime-import guard only recognises ESM `import … from`, so a `require()` of a source-direct workspace package — the exact idiom already used four times in apps/api/src — passes the guard while crashing `node dist/main.js` at boot.
findings.detail:
State path: `collectRuntimeWorkspacePackages` (line 53) scans every non-spec `.ts`/`.tsx` under `apps/api/src` with a single pattern, line 55: `/(^|\n)\s*import\s+(?!type\b)[^;]*from\s+["'](@routeflow\/[^"']+)["']/g`. It requires the literal token `from`, so it matches none of the three CommonJS-emitting forms TypeScript accepts in this codebase: `const X = require("@routeflow/types")`, `import X = require("@routeflow/types")`, and `await import("@routeflow/types")`. The assertion at line 77 is `expect(imported).toEqual(["@routeflow/pricing"])`, so an undetected package simply never enters the array and the test is GREEN.

This is not hypothetical for this repo: `git grep 'require("' -- apps/api/src/**/*.ts` returns four live production call sites using exactly that idiom — apps/api/src/billing/stripe.service.ts:8, apps/api/src/payment-requests/provider/stripe-payment-provider.ts:18, apps/api/src/stripe-connect/provider/stripe-connect-oauth.provider.ts:14 (`const Stripe = require("stripe")`) and apps/api/src/storage/compress.util.ts:2 (`const sharp = require("sharp")`). A developer following that established pattern writes `const { OrderStatus } = require("@routeflow/types")` in a service; `tsc --noEmit` and ts-jest both pass (as the file's own header at lines 1-14 explains), `nest build` emits `require("@routeflow/types")` verbatim into `apps/api/dist`, and `node dist/main.js` dies at startup parsing raw TypeScript — the whole API down, not one module. Both describes in this file report clean.

The file's own doc comment at line 38 asserts the coverage it does not have: "a plain `import ... from` (or a `require`) is not [erased]" — the parenthetical is written into the comment but never into the regex. The first (pre-existing) describe shares the blind spot; this PR's new T4/R6 describe inherits it wholesale, which matters more now because `@routeflow/pricing` is the first workspace package the API is *allowed* to import at runtime, so the guard is the only thing distinguishing the allowed compiled package from a boot-killing source-direct one.

Evidence gathered this session: I read the file in full; the regex at line 55 and the `expect(...).toEqual(["@routeflow/pricing"])` at line 77 are quoted verbatim above; the four `require("...")` call sites came from a git grep over apps/api/src excluding spec files.
findings.fixHint: Extend the scan to the CommonJS/dynamic forms as well as `import … from` — e.g. add patterns for `require("@routeflow/…")`, `import X = require("@routeflow/…")` and `import("@routeflow/…")` — and feed all matches into the same normalised package set. Fix the same gap in the first describe (line ~40) so its comment at line 38 becomes true. Deciding whether a dynamic `import()` should be allowed (it is still a runtime require under CJS emit) is the judgment call.
findings.decision: The regex at line 55 requires the literal `from` token, so `require("@routeflow/x")`, `import X = require(...)` and dynamic `import()` never enter the array and the `toEqual(["@routeflow/pricing"])` assertion stays green; the codebase already uses `require()` four times in api/src, so the idiom is live. No current offender exists, so it is a tripwire blind spot (same class as the confirmed no-mirrors T3 gap), not a shipped breakage — fix by extending the pattern to the three CJS forms.

findings.summary: The `lint` task is the only task type with no `^build` edge, so ESLint's type-aware program for api/web/mobile can run against a stale or entirely absent `packages/pricing/dist/index.d.ts`.
findings.detail:
Verified with `npx turbo run lint --dry=json` in the worktree: `@routeflow/api#lint <- ["@routeflow/pricing#lint","@routeflow/types#lint"]`, `@routeflow/web#lint <- ["@routeflow/pricing#lint","@routeflow/types#lint","@routeflow/ui#lint"]`, `@routeflow/mobile#lint <- ["@routeflow/eslint-config#lint","@routeflow/pricing#lint","@routeflow/types#lint"]` — `@routeflow/pricing#build` appears in none of them. For contrast, `npx turbo run check-types test build --dry=json` shows the edge present everywhere else: `@routeflow/api#check-types <- ["@routeflow/pricing#build",…]`, `@routeflow/api#test <- ["@routeflow/pricing#build",…]`, `@routeflow/api#build <- ["@routeflow/pricing#build",…]` (same for web and mobile). turbo.json:45-48 declares `"lint": { "dependsOn": ["^lint"], "outputs": [] }` while :87-90 declares `"check-types": { "dependsOn": ["^build", "^check-types"] }` with the comment "`^build` first: @routeflow/pricing is a COMPILED workspace package, so its dependents cannot typecheck until its dist/*.d.ts exists" — the same reasoning applies to lint and was not carried over. Note `@routeflow/pricing#lint` is `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (packages/pricing/package.json), which needs no dist of its own, so that edge buys nothing here.

Failure path A (absent dist): the root `clean` script is `turbo run clean && rm -rf node_modules`, and `@routeflow/pricing`'s `clean` is `node -e "require('fs').rmSync('dist',…)"`. After a `turbo run clean` (or any checkout where `npm ci` ran with `--ignore-scripts`), `npm run lint` runs `@routeflow/api#lint` = `eslint "{src,apps,libs,test}/**/*.ts"` with `tseslint.configs.recommendedTypeChecked` + `parserOptions: { projectService: true }` (apps/api/eslint.config.mjs:21, :31). `@routeflow/pricing` resolves through `exports["."].types = "./dist/index.d.ts"`, which is gone, so every one of the pricing imports across the API degrades to `any`. Because the typed rules are all severity `"warn"` in that config (`no-unsafe-argument`, `no-unsafe-assignment`, `no-unsafe-member-access`, `no-unsafe-return`, `no-unsafe-call`) and no `--max-warnings` is set, lint still exits 0 — the type-aware half of the money call sites' lint silently stops meaning anything, with no signal.

Failure path B (torn read): `npm run verify` is `… && turbo run check-types lint test --concurrency=2 && …` and CI runs exactly that command on a runner with no turbo cache (.github/workflows/ci.yml:~244, and the deliberate no-cache note at :236). With no lint→build edge, `@routeflow/{api,web,mobile}#lint` can be scheduled concurrently with the cold `@routeflow/pricing#build`, i.e. ESLint's TS program can read `dist/index.d.ts` while `tsc` is truncating and rewriting it. Same silent degradation, but nondeterministic.

This never turns a red into a green on its own (check-types carries the real type gate and does have the edge), which is why I am filing it minor rather than major.
findings.fixHint: Add `"^build"` to the `lint` task's `dependsOn` in turbo.json:45-48, matching `check-types` at :87-90, so it reads `"dependsOn": ["^build", "^lint"]`.
findings.decision: The dry-run graph shows `lint` is the only task without a `^build` edge while check-types/test/build all carry it deliberately; a type-aware ESLint program for api/web/mobile therefore resolves `@routeflow/pricing` types from whatever `dist/index.d.ts` happens to exist. Postinstall covers fresh `npm ci`, so the exposure is the edit-then-lint loop or an `--ignore-scripts` install — stale-signature or `any`-degraded lint, not a runtime fault. Add `^build` to lint's dependsOn.

findings.summary: `@routeflow/pricing#dev` and `@routeflow/pricing#build` have no ordering edge but compile the same project into the same `dist/`, so `npm run dev` starts two concurrent tsc writers over the files `nest start --watch` / `next dev` are about to require.
findings.detail:
Verified with `npx turbo run dev --dry=json`: `@routeflow/pricing#dev <- ["@routeflow/typescript-config#build"]` and `@routeflow/pricing#build <- ["@routeflow/typescript-config#build"]` — neither depends on the other, and `@routeflow/pricing#build` is pulled into the same run because `@routeflow/api#dev <- ["@routeflow/pricing#build","@routeflow/types#build"]`, `@routeflow/web#dev <- ["@routeflow/pricing#build",…]`, `@routeflow/mobile#dev <- ["@routeflow/pricing#build",…]`.

Both tasks target byte-for-byte the same output: packages/pricing/package.json declares `"build": "tsc -p tsconfig.build.json"` and `"dev": "tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --watch --preserveWatchOutput"`, and tsconfig.build.json sets `"outDir": "dist"`. Turbo starts persistent tasks as soon as their declared deps are satisfied, so on `npm run dev` the one-shot build and the watcher's initial emit run at the same instant, each truncating and rewriting packages/pricing/dist/{index,pricing,tier-pricing}.{js,d.ts,*.map} with no lock between them.

Concrete failure: `npm run dev` on a cold cache. `@routeflow/api#dev` (`nest start --watch`) and `@routeflow/web#dev` (`next dev`) are gated only on `@routeflow/pricing#build`, so the moment that one-shot exits they begin resolving `@routeflow/pricing` → `main: "./dist/index.js"` while the watcher may still be mid-emit on the same three files. A torn read surfaces as `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input` from the API's `require("@routeflow/pricing")` or a Next module-parse error — nondeterministic, and "fixed" by restarting, which is the worst shape for a dev-loop bug. The same collision exists in the other direction when `@routeflow/pricing#build` is a cache HIT: turbo restores its `dist/**` outputs (the generic `build` task at turbo.json:38 declares `"outputs": [… "dist/**" …]`) into a directory the watcher is concurrently writing.

This is new with this PR: `@routeflow/pricing` is the first workspace package that has both a real `build` and a real `dev`, both emitting to the same outDir. I did not reproduce the torn read (it would require running the persistent dev graph); the evidence is the missing edge in the dry-run graph plus the two scripts' identical `-p tsconfig.build.json` target.
findings.fixHint: Either give the package's dev task its own build edge (`"@routeflow/pricing#dev": { "dependsOn": ["build"] }`) so the watcher only starts after the one-shot emit, or drop the package's `dev` script entirely and rely on the `^build` edge the app dev tasks already carry. Which one is right depends on whether a pricing edit should hot-rebuild during `npm run dev`.
findings.decision: `@routeflow/pricing#dev` (`tsc --watch`) and `@routeflow/pricing#build` (`tsc`) have no ordering edge and both are scheduled by `npm run dev` because the app dev tasks depend on `^build`; both emit the same files into `dist/` at the same instant. tsc's writes are not atomic, so a torn read by `nest start --watch` is possible, but the two emits are byte-identical and the window is milliseconds, so this is a low-probability hazard in the host loop. Make the watcher depend on the one-shot build, or drop the package's `dev` task.

findings.summary: `@routeflow/api#test` now asserts on `apps/mobile/jest.config.js`, but that file is in neither `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` nor `globalDependencies`, so turbo can replay a cached green for the assertion that guards mobile's pricing module mapping.
findings.detail:
This PR added an assertion in apps/api/src/common/no-runtime-workspace-imports.spec.ts:104-113 — "apps/mobile/jest.config.js moduleNameMapper resolves ^@routeflow/pricing$ to packages/pricing/src/index.ts" — which reads `join(SRC_ROOT, "..", "..", "mobile", "jest.config.js")` (line 105) with `readFileSync` (line 106). That spec runs under `@routeflow/api#test`, whose inputs are the generic `test` task's `["$TURBO_DEFAULT$"]` (turbo.json:49-57). `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` covers only the task's own package directory (`apps/api`), and turbo.json:28-33 `globalDependencies` lists only `package-lock.json`, `package.json`, `apps/*/package.json`, `packages/*/package.json` — `apps/mobile/jest.config.js` matches none of them.

Concrete failure: someone edits apps/mobile/jest.config.js to delete or retarget `"^@routeflow/pricing$": "<rootDir>/../../packages/pricing/src/index.ts"` (a plausible edit — "make the mobile tests use dist so they match production") and changes nothing under apps/api and no manifest or lockfile. `@routeflow/api#test`'s hash is unchanged, so `turbo run test` (via `npm run verify`, which the pre-push hook runs on every push per .husky/pre-push) replays a cached PASS and the assertion that should have gone red never executes. `@routeflow/mobile#test` also stays green, because with the mapper gone jest resolves `@routeflow/pricing` through node_modules to the plain-CommonJS `dist/index.js`, which needs no transform. Both lanes report green while R6's mapping is gone.

This is the same stale-cache class the PR handled correctly one task over — turbo.json:58-79 adds an explicit `@routeflow/pricing#test` inputs block precisely because "A package's $TURBO_DEFAULT$ only ever covers its OWN directory" — but the T4/R6 assertions that reach out of their package were placed in apps/api rather than packages/pricing, so they sit outside that block's protection. I am filing it minor, not major, because CI is deliberately cache-free (.github/workflows/ci.yml:236 "no actions/cache of .turbo, so every task genuinely executes on a fresh runner"), so the false green is confined to warm local runs and the pre-push gate.
findings.fixHint: Either move the two cross-app mapper assertions (no-runtime-workspace-imports.spec.ts:96-113) into packages/pricing, where the `@routeflow/pricing#test` inputs block at turbo.json:58-79 already hashes `$TURBO_ROOT$/apps/mobile/**`, or add an `@routeflow/api#test` inputs entry hashing `$TURBO_ROOT$/apps/mobile/jest.config.js`. The first keeps the deleted `@routeflow/api#test` block deleted, which is what R3 intended — that trade-off is the judgment call.
findings.decision: The new api-side assertion reads `apps/mobile/jest.config.js`, which is outside `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` for apps/api and not in `globalDependencies`, so turbo can replay a cached green after that file is edited — the same stale-cache class already confirmed for `@routeflow/pricing#test`, but a distinct file/edge. The guarded mapping only affects whether mobile tests run against src or dist (dist still resolves via the symlink), so coverage degrades silently rather than anything breaking. Add the file to an `@routeflow/api#test` inputs block alongside the pricing#test fix.

confirmedFindings.summary: Package p4-wiring is partial
confirmedFindings.detail:
1. DOCKERFILES — deliberate deviation from the plan's "one `COPY packages/pricing/package.json packages/pricing/` line". In BOTH Dockerfiles `RUN npm ci` (apps/api:24, apps/web:26 — verified by grep) runs BEFORE `COPY packages/ packages/` (apps/api:27, apps/web:42). The new root postinstall runs during that `npm ci`, so a manifest-only copy would leave packages/pricing with no tsconfig.build.json and no src/ — `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` exits non-zero ("specified path does not exist" / "no inputs were found") and BOTH images would fail to build. apps/web additionally re-triggers postinstall at :39 (`npm install --force --no-save react@18…`), also before the source copy. I therefore wrote `COPY packages/pricing/ packages/pricing/` (still one COPY line each, in the manifest layer, with a comment explaining why). `.dockerignore` has `**/dist`, so no host dist/ enters the context. This is a gap in spec R4 as written, not a discretionary style choice.

2. p1 (`p1-package-skeleton`) HAS NOT LANDED — packages/pricing/package.json is still the 3-field stub the test package created ({name, private, version}); there is no `build` script, no tsconfig.json/tsconfig.build.json, no src/index.ts, no .gitignore. Consequences, all verified this session:
   - The plan's prove step could NOT be run. `npm run build -w @routeflow/pricing` fails with `npm error Missing script: "build"`, so `cd apps/api && node -e "…Object.keys(require('@routeflow/pricing')).length"` (expect >= 38) was not executed. UNVERIFIED.
   - A full `npm install` would abort at the new root postinstall. I ran `npm install --ignore-scripts` instead — a REAL reify (node_modules/@routeflow/pricing symlink created, package-lock.json rewritten), NOT `--package-lock-only` (L-032). Lifecycle scripts skipped were the root postinstall (would fail) and apps/api's `prisma generate` (its client was already generated in this worktree).
   - The committed lockfile WILL need regenerating once p1 lands: p1's package.json adds devDependencies (jest, ts-jest, typescript, @types/jest) that change the lock. The current `packages/pricing` lock entry is `{"version":"0.0.1"}` with no `name`, reflecting the stub manifest.

3. Install ran through `npx npm@10.8.0` (the repo's pinned `packageManager`), not the local npm 11.9.0 / node 24. The local npm produced 342 lines of `dev` -> `devOptional` metadata drift (the "foreign npm" drift documented in turbo.json's own comment); I reverted that and reinstalled with the pinned npm, giving a clean 11-line lockfile diff.

4. Per instruction 5 I did NOT run any test suite, so T1 and T4 were not executed as Jest runs (packages/pricing also has no jest devDependency yet, so its suite cannot run until p1). I verified their config-level assertions by reading the same values the specs read (see notes).

confirmedFindings.summary: The mobile image never copies packages/pricing, so the new root postinstall fails inside its `RUN npm ci` and the mobile Railway build breaks.
confirmedFindings.detail: apps/mobile/Dockerfile's manifest layer (lines 12-20) copies only packages/{config,eslint-config,types,typescript-config,ui}/package.json plus apps/mobile/package.json — there is no packages/pricing copy at all — and then runs `RUN npm ci` at line 25 (the full `COPY packages/ packages/` is at line 28, AFTER the install). This PR adds a root `postinstall` of `npm run build -w @routeflow/pricing`, which npm executes during that `npm ci`. I reproduced the exact failure in a scratch workspace root with the same `workspaces: ["apps/*","packages/*"]` glob and the same postinstall, minus packages/pricing: `npm error No workspaces found: --workspace=@routeflow/pricing`, real exit code 1. A failing postinstall fails `npm ci`, so the builder layer aborts and the mobile image never builds. (apps/mobile/package.json also now declares `"@routeflow/pricing": "*"`, so `npm ci` would likely refuse the out-of-sync tree even before the script runs.) Spec R4 and build-plan p4 enumerate only apps/api/Dockerfile and apps/web/Dockerfile; apps/mobile/Dockerfile is the third `npm ci` site in the repo and was never touched (apps/db-backup/Dockerfile is postgres-only, no npm — checked).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Mirror the edit already made to apps/api/Dockerfile and apps/web/Dockerfile: before `RUN npm ci` (line 25) add `COPY packages/pricing/ packages/pricing/` and change `COPY packages/typescript-config/package.json packages/typescript-config/` to `COPY packages/typescript-config/ packages/typescript-config/` (packages/pricing/tsconfig.json extends @routeflow/typescript-config/base.json). confirmedFindings.summary: The golden money table can go silently vacuous: if golden.fixtures.ts ever fails to resolve, all eight fixture tables register zero tests and the suite still passes.
confirmedFindings.detail: `guardedRequire("./golden.fixtures")` (line 29) swallows any resolution error and returns `{}`; `table()` then returns `[]` for every name, and `itEachFixture()` (lines 54-57) deliberately registers NO test when the array is empty. So a rename, move, or syntax error in golden.fixtures.ts drops ROUND_MONEY_FIXTURES, COMPUTE_LINE_SUBTOTAL_FIXTURES, APPLY_BEST_PROMOTION_FIXTURES, PRORATE_LINE_SUBTOTAL_FIXTURES, PRORATE_EDGE_FIXTURES, TIER_PRICE_FIXTURES, CASCADE_TIER_PRICE_FIXTURES and NORMALIZE_BOXES_PIECES_FIXTURES from the run, and `packages/pricing` still reports green off the 5 remaining hand-written cases — for the file the PR designates as THE golden money oracle. Note the sibling tripwire src/no-mirrors.spec.ts:130-136 does carry an explicit anti-vacuity assertion, so the pattern is established in this same package.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either drop the guarded requires now that the module and fixtures exist (plain imports), or add an anti-vacuity test asserting each of the eight tables has length > 0 (and that `typeof mod.roundMoney === "function"`).

confirmedFindings.summary: golden.spec.ts's itEachFixture registers ZERO tests when a fixture table is missing or empty, so the golden money table can silently lose 90% of its coverage and still report PASS.
confirmedFindings.detail: `itEachFixture` does `const rows = table(name); if (rows.length > 0) it.each(rows)(...)`, and `table()` returns `[]` for any name that is not an array on the fixtures module. Nothing asserts a table is non-empty. Proven this session: I ran golden.spec.ts with `moduleNameMapper` pointing `./golden.fixtures` at an empty module — the suite reported `Tests: 5 passed, 5 total` and `PASS`, down from 51 passed on the real fixtures. So renaming/deleting `ROUND_MONEY_FIXTURES` (or any of the other seven tables) in golden.fixtures.ts, or a typo in one of the eight name strings in this spec, drops the entire REG-B122 / REG-B109 / REG-B50 golden table to zero executed assertions with a green suite. T2 is the primary proof for R2 ("no pricing body may change"), so this is the one guard that must not be able to go vacuous.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add an explicit non-vacuity assertion per table (e.g. an `it("TABLE is non-empty")` for each of the eight names, or make itEachFixture register a failing test when rows.length === 0 instead of registering nothing).

confirmedFindings.summary: The R2 body-diff verifier now exits 0 having compared zero symbols, and it also exits 0 when symbols DIFFER — its green is indistinguishable from "nothing was checked".

Because the typed rules are all severity `"warn"` in that config (`no-unsafe-argument`, `no-unsafe-assignment`, `no-unsafe-member-access`, `no-unsafe-return`, `no-unsafe-call`) and no `--max-warnings` is set, lint still exits 0 — the type-aware half of the money call sites' lint silently stops meaning anything, with no signal.

Failure path B (torn read): `npm run verify` is `… && turbo run check-types lint test --concurrency=2 && …` and CI runs exactly that command on a runner with no turbo cache (.github/workflows/ci.yml:~244, and the deliberate no-cache note at :236). With no lint→build edge, `@routeflow/{api,web,mobile}#lint` can be scheduled concurrently with the cold `@routeflow/pricing#build`, i.e. ESLint's TS program can read `dist/index.d.ts` while `tsc` is truncating and rewriting it. Same silent degradation, but nondeterministic.

This never turns a red into a green on its own (check-types carries the real type gate and does have the edge), which is why I am filing it minor rather than major.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add `"^build"` to the `lint` task's `dependsOn` in turbo.json:45-48, matching `check-types` at :87-90, so it reads `"dependsOn": ["^build", "^lint"]`.
remainingFindings.decision: The dry-run graph shows `lint` is the only task without a `^build` edge while check-types/test/build all carry it deliberately; a type-aware ESLint program for api/web/mobile therefore resolves `@routeflow/pricing` types from whatever `dist/index.d.ts` happens to exist. Postinstall covers fresh `npm ci`, so the exposure is the edit-then-lint loop or an `--ignore-scripts` install — stale-signature or `any`-degraded lint, not a runtime fault. Add `^build` to lint's dependsOn.

remainingFindings.summary: `@routeflow/pricing#dev` and `@routeflow/pricing#build` have no ordering edge but compile the same project into the same `dist/`, so `npm run dev` starts two concurrent tsc writers over the files `nest start --watch` / `next dev` are about to require.
remainingFindings.detail:
Verified with `npx turbo run dev --dry=json`: `@routeflow/pricing#dev <- ["@routeflow/typescript-config#build"]` and `@routeflow/pricing#build <- ["@routeflow/typescript-config#build"]` — neither depends on the other, and `@routeflow/pricing#build` is pulled into the same run because `@routeflow/api#dev <- ["@routeflow/pricing#build","@routeflow/types#build"]`, `@routeflow/web#dev <- ["@routeflow/pricing#build",…]`, `@routeflow/mobile#dev <- ["@routeflow/pricing#build",…]`.

Both tasks target byte-for-byte the same output: packages/pricing/package.json declares `"build": "tsc -p tsconfig.build.json"` and `"dev": "tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --watch --preserveWatchOutput"`, and tsconfig.build.json sets `"outDir": "dist"`. Turbo starts persistent tasks as soon as their declared deps are satisfied, so on `npm run dev` the one-shot build and the watcher's initial emit run at the same instant, each truncating and rewriting packages/pricing/dist/{index,pricing,tier-pricing}.{js,d.ts,*.map} with no lock between them.

Concrete failure: `npm run dev` on a cold cache. `@routeflow/api#dev` (`nest start --watch`) and `@routeflow/web#dev` (`next dev`) are gated only on `@routeflow/pricing#build`, so the moment that one-shot exits they begin resolving `@routeflow/pricing` → `main: "./dist/index.js"` while the watcher may still be mid-emit on the same three files. A torn read surfaces as `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input` from the API's `require("@routeflow/pricing")` or a Next module-parse error — nondeterministic, and "fixed" by restarting, which is the worst shape for a dev-loop bug. The same collision exists in the other direction when `@routeflow/pricing#build` is a cache HIT: turbo restores its `dist/**` outputs (the generic `build` task at turbo.json:38 declares `"outputs": [… "dist/**" …]`) into a directory the watcher is concurrently writing.

This is new with this PR: `@routeflow/pricing` is the first workspace package that has both a real `build` and a real `dev`, both emitting to the same outDir. I did not reproduce the torn read (it would require running the persistent dev graph); the evidence is the missing edge in the dry-run graph plus the two scripts' identical `-p tsconfig.build.json` target.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either give the package's dev task its own build edge (`"@routeflow/pricing#dev": { "dependsOn": ["build"] }`) so the watcher only starts after the one-shot emit, or drop the package's `dev` script entirely and rely on the `^build` edge the app dev tasks already carry. Which one is right depends on whether a pricing edit should hot-rebuild during `npm run dev`.
remainingFindings.decision: `@routeflow/pricing#dev` (`tsc --watch`) and `@routeflow/pricing#build` (`tsc`) have no ordering edge and both are scheduled by `npm run dev` because the app dev tasks depend on `^build`; both emit the same files into `dist/` at the same instant. tsc's writes are not atomic, so a torn read by `nest start --watch` is possible, but the two emits are byte-identical and the window is milliseconds, so this is a low-probability hazard in the host loop. Make the watcher depend on the one-shot build, or drop the package's `dev` task.

remainingFindings.summary: `@routeflow/api#test` now asserts on `apps/mobile/jest.config.js`, but that file is in neither `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` nor `globalDependencies`, so turbo can replay a cached green for the assertion that guards mobile's pricing module mapping.
remainingFindings.detail:
This PR added an assertion in apps/api/src/common/no-runtime-workspace-imports.spec.ts:104-113 — "apps/mobile/jest.config.js moduleNameMapper resolves ^@routeflow/pricing$ to packages/pricing/src/index.ts" — which reads `join(SRC_ROOT, "..", "..", "mobile", "jest.config.js")` (line 105) with `readFileSync` (line 106). That spec runs under `@routeflow/api#test`, whose inputs are the generic `test` task's `["$TURBO_DEFAULT$"]` (turbo.json:49-57). `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` covers only the task's own package directory (`apps/api`), and turbo.json:28-33 `globalDependencies` lists only `package-lock.json`, `package.json`, `apps/*/package.json`, `packages/*/package.json` — `apps/mobile/jest.config.js` matches none of them.

Concrete failure: someone edits apps/mobile/jest.config.js to delete or retarget `"^@routeflow/pricing$": "<rootDir>/../../packages/pricing/src/index.ts"` (a plausible edit — "make the mobile tests use dist so they match production") and changes nothing under apps/api and no manifest or lockfile. `@routeflow/api#test`'s hash is unchanged, so `turbo run test` (via `npm run verify`, which the pre-push hook runs on every push per .husky/pre-push) replays a cached PASS and the assertion that should have gone red never executes. `@routeflow/mobile#test` also stays green, because with the mapper gone jest resolves `@routeflow/pricing` through node_modules to the plain-CommonJS `dist/index.js`, which needs no transform. Both lanes report green while R6's mapping is gone.

This is the same stale-cache class the PR handled correctly one task over — turbo.json:58-79 adds an explicit `@routeflow/pricing#test` inputs block precisely because "A package's $TURBO_DEFAULT$ only ever covers its OWN directory" — but the T4/R6 assertions that reach out of their package were placed in apps/api rather than packages/pricing, so they sit outside that block's protection. I am filing it minor, not major, because CI is deliberately cache-free (.github/workflows/ci.yml:236 "no actions/cache of .turbo, so every task genuinely executes on a fresh runner"), so the false green is confined to warm local runs and the pre-push gate.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either move the two cross-app mapper assertions (no-runtime-workspace-imports.spec.ts:96-113) into packages/pricing, where the `@routeflow/pricing#test` inputs block at turbo.json:58-79 already hashes `$TURBO_ROOT$/apps/mobile/**`, or add an `@routeflow/api#test` inputs entry hashing `$TURBO_ROOT$/apps/mobile/jest.config.js`. The first keeps the deleted `@routeflow/api#test` block deleted, which is what R3 intended — that trade-off is the judgment call.
remainingFindings.decision: The new api-side assertion reads `apps/mobile/jest.config.js`, which is outside `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` for apps/api and not in `globalDependencies`, so turbo can replay a cached green after that file is edited — the same stale-cache class already confirmed for `@routeflow/pricing#test`, but a distinct file/edge. The guarded mapping only affects whether mobile tests run against src or dist (dist still resolves via the symlink), so coverage degrades silently rather than anything breaking. Add the file to an `@routeflow/api#test` inputs block alongside the pricing#test fix.
